vo.text: A city of palaces, churches and bell towers, standing in the middle of the sea. Here is the strange part. Underneath it, there is almost no solid ground.
About fifteen hundred years ago, people running from war hid on small muddy islands in a lagoon: a shallow bay, protected from the sea by a long strip of sand.
Mud is a terrible place to build. Put a stone house on it, and the house slowly sinks, like a spoon in pudding.
So the Venetians did something clever. They hammered wooden poles straight down into the mud. Millions of them.
Each pole was a tree trunk, sharpened at the end, of oak, alder or pine. They packed them tight, side by side, all the way down to a harder layer of clay.
On top of the poles they laid thick wooden boards. On the boards, waterproof white stone. And only then, the walls.
One church alone, Santa Maria della Sa-lootay, stands on more than a million of these poles.
vo.script: One church alone, Santa Maria della Salute, stands on more than a million of these poles.
vo.why: spoken spelling so the free voice says sa-LOO-tay, not the English word salute

vo.text: But wait. Wood in water rots, right? Not down there. Deep in the mud there is almost no air, and the tiny creatures that eat wood need air to live.
So for hundreds of years the poles have stayed strong, and minerals in the water have soaked into them and made them even harder.
So why is Venice sinking? Two reasons. First, the mud under the city is still being squeezed, very slowly, by everything standing on top of it.
Second, the sea is rising. A little more water every year, a slightly lower city.
In the last century, factories nearby made it worse. They pumped water up from under the ground, the mud squeezed down, and the city dropped faster. Then the pumping was stopped.
Today, on the worst days, the sea pours into the squares, and people walk to work on raised wooden walkways.

So Venice built a wall that hides under the sea. Seventy-eight giant gates lie on the seabed at the three openings of the lagoon. When a big tide comes, air is pumped in, and they float up to hold the sea back.
They rose for real for the first time in October twenty twenty. The squares stayed dry.
vo.script: They rose for real for the first time in October 2020. The squares stayed dry.
vo.why: spoken spelling: twenty twenty, not two thousand and twenty

vo.text: A city standing on an upside down forest, in the middle of the sea, for fifteen hundred years. Just keep your feet dry.
